cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Mobile tile
cases.question: What has Brad built on mobile?
cases.answer: Brad has built mobile work across several roles. At Bottle Rocket, Brad shipped native Android apps in Java and Kotlin for brands including Coca-Cola Freestyle, AskPETMD, Starwood SPG and Chewy. At BookShout, Brad modernized the Android app with Kotlin, Architecture Components, Data Binding, RxJava 2, OkHttp and Retrofit. At RealPage, Brad led Android development across a suite of real-estate management apps. At Bleacher Report, Brad built and maintained Android product experiences for a high-traffic sports media platform. At Hopper, Brad co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS. Brad also built VINDecoded, where Android has 1M+ downloads (4.5 stars) and iOS has 400K+ (4.7 stars).

cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Full-stack tile
cases.question: What has Brad built across the stack?
cases.answer: Brad has built across mobile, web, backend and AI work. On Android, Brad shipped native Android apps in Java and Kotlin for brands including Coca-Cola Freestyle, AskPETMD, Starwood SPG and Chewy. At Hopper, Brad co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS, and delivered Disruption Assistance end to end: the RFC and ADR, stakeholder alignment, new services on Terraform-provisioned GCP, backend APIs, a payment flow with rewards points, offer generation and Redis caching, and the React front end. For VINDecoded, Brad re-platformed from AngularJS/Cordova to a React/TypeScript web app, native Android and iOS apps, and a Node.js/TypeScript API backed by SQL, Firebase, Azure and cloud analytics.

cases.answer: The phrase comes from Brad's résumé entry for VINDecoded, which describes it as a profitable vehicle-history and research platform for shoppers, owners and sellers. For more detail on the review step, the essay on tests and a second reader says that when the code is done, a second agent reviews it with fresh context and only read tools, so it can't quietly fix what it finds. On releases, merging to master deploys nothing. A release happens only when Brad asks for one.
